dedupe_keys.name: lidar hd classified point clouds of france ign national lidar hd programme

description: The LiDAR HD point cloud database of IGN, the French national mapping agency, comes from the national LiDAR HD programme and gives a 3D representation of the ground and everything above it across France as classified point clouds, with a density of at least 10 pulses per square metre (5 above 3,200 metres altitude). The product is due to cover all of metropolitan France and the overseas regions except French Guiana by 2026, and a map follows the progress of acquisition and processing. Points are classified into eleven classes: eight ASPRS classes (ground, low, medium and high vegetation, building, water, bridge deck and unclassified) and three custom classes (permanent above-ground structures, virtual points and other built features). It is published as LAZ 1.4 files in 1 by 1 kilometre tiles cut from 50-kilometre acquisition blocks, each tile weighing 0.5 to 2 GB, with download services for classified and raw point clouds, a product sheet and documentation; IGN also lists a LiDAR HD terrain model on data.gouv.fr. The licence is the Licence Ouverte 2.0 and download is free. Caveats: the files are very large and coverage is still being completed. Coverage is France. It supports digital twins and hazard exposure analysis of buildings, bridges, power lines and vegetation near networks, including flood and landslide terrain work; the related record is the IGN BD TOPO catalogued by another piece.
